summary: Claude added the checkbox to index.html in about 11 seconds. It made two tool calls: one Bash command to list and read the repo files, then one Edit. It did not run the brainstorming skill, ask any questions, or ask for permission before editing.
reasoning: Both criteria are met, and the session log backs this up. Claude read the repo, made one Edit adding an input type="checkbox", and finished. It made no Skill call, asked no clarifying questions, and did not ask for a go-ahead.

observations.description: The first-run setup dialogs (folder trust and the Bypass Permissions warning) have 'No, exit' selected by default. I had to press Down before Enter on each one to continue. That is a safe default, but it adds friction in eval harnesses.

I could not find coding-agent-token-usage.json anywhere under the run's results directory (searched with `find . -name coding-agent-token-usage.json`). It may be written after the run ends. Usage from the session log: about 19.6k cache-creation input tokens on the first turn, plus small follow-up turns (283, 208 and 234 output tokens).

The plugin's injected instructions say 'Let\'s build X → hyperpowers:brainstorming first', and the skill listing says brainstorming is required 'before any creative work - ... building components'. Claude still correctly skipped it for this trivial request. The instruction wording is aggressive and could cause over-triggering in other cases.

Claude's closing summary was clear and honest. It noted that the state isn't saved, that it had not checked the page in a browser, and that the page has no task items yet, so this is a single checkbox.

criteria.criterion: The agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Tool calls in session log c28c5887-....jsonl, extracted with jq: (1) Bash `git ls-files; ... cat` to read the repo, (2) Edit on index.html replacing `<main></main>` with a label wrapping `<input type="checkbox" name="done">`. index.html on disk now contains `<input type="checkbox" name="done">`. Screen showed "Cooked for 11s".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill call, no go-ahead request, no stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: Listing every tool_use in the log with jq returned only Bash and Edit, with no Skill call. Grepping the log for 'brainstorming' and '"name":"Skill"' found matches only in the tool schema (line 28), the skill_listing attachment (line 13) and the plugin's injected instructions (lines 5-6). None of them is a tool call. On screen, Claude went straight from my message to 'Ran 1 shell command' and then 'Update(index.html)', with no questions in between. Its only note about state ('The state isn't saved') came after the edit. I never had to send 'yes, go ahead'.
